items.title: A monumental bronze teddy bear surrounded by flowers is taking over South Beach sands for Miami Art Week
items.text:
See the giant bronze teddy bear on South Beach at the Ritz-Carlton from December 1 through 6 as part of Miami Art Week.

Talk about a bear-y unique sight to see during Art Week! This December, a black-patinated bronze teddy bear is set to lie on the sand outside of The Ritz-Carlton, South Beach. Titled Poor Teddy in Memoriam, it'll be on public view for the first time beginning December 1st, and anyone can walk up to it for free!The sculpture is actually the centerpiece of The Perfect Trade-Off, a solo exhibition by American conceptual artist Rachel Lee Hovnanian. The bear will rest on the beachfront with flowers around it — like a memorial — and its contrast black color standing out against the beach.Rendering of Poor Teddy in Memoriam by Rachel Lee HovnanianWhere to catch the large-scale worksThe exhibition spreads across the hotel's public spaces and the beach. Four works look at how technology and artificial intelligence shape human connection, imagination and attention. Additionally, what may be lost as our lives become increasingly personalized and screen-mediated.These are the highlights:Poor Teddy in Memoriam: A monumental teddy bear on the beachfront exploring childhood imagination in the digital age.Dinner for Ten: Debuting in the hotel lobby, an elaborate table for 10 shows nine chairs occupied by monitors showing guests absorbed on their phones, leaving one seat for the viewer.FMLMBD (F**k My Life My Battery’s Dead): A vintage Piaggio Ape converted into a working phone-charging station, parked outdoors at the hotel.Motherboard (Jupiter): A reflective work connecting Hovnanian’s earlier examinations of digital identity with today’s questions around attention, connection and AI.FMLMBD ChargingTruckPlan your visitThe Ritz-Carlton, South Beach is located at 1 Lincoln Road, Miami Beach, a short walk from the Miami Beach Convention Center. That makes it an easy stop between fair visits! The works are open to the public through December 6th, during the hotel's regular operating hours.Miami Art Week runs November 30th to December 6th. If you're looking for more installations to catch for free during the art-filled affair, check out our roundup of free Art Week happenings here.See also: Everything you need to know about Art Basel Miami Beach 2026: Tickets, dates and can’t-miss satellite events
items.desc: See the giant bronze teddy bear on South Beach at the Ritz-Carlton from December 1 through 6 as part of Miami Art Week.

items.title: Deputies search for missing 31-year-old woman from SW Miami-Dade
items.text:
SOUTHWEST MIAMI-DADE, FLA. (WSVN) - The Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Office is seeking the public’s help in finding a missing woman from Southwest Miami-Dade.
Deputies said that 31-year-old Michelle A. Monserrat was last seen in the 9300 block of Southwest 152nd Street on Friday.
She was last seen wearing a white t-shirt, black shorts, and black sandals at the time of her disappearance.
Monserrat has brown eyes and black hair, weighs 180 pounds and stands 5 feet, 7 inches tall.
Detectives said Monserrat suffers from schizophrenia and anxiety disorder.
Anyone with information on the above subject and/or case should contact Deputy O. Tellez, at 305-715-3300 (Office), 305-715-3252 (Desk), email u304578@mdso.com or Crime Stoppers at 305-471-TIPS (8477).

items.title: Tornado warning cancelled as storm rolls through Miami-Dade, Broward
items.text:
The NBC6 South Florida News streaming channel plays local South Florida news 24 hours a day, seven days a week.
A tornado warning has expired after going into effect in Broward and Miami-Dade counties on Saturday, according to the National Weather Service.
The warning was in effect due to a severe thunderstorm located over the area. It was cancelled at around 12:20 p.m.
What you should do in case of a tornado warning: Take cover, and move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a sturdy building. Avoid windows. If you are outdoors, in a mobile home, or in a vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter and protect yourself from flying debris.
The NWS advises that strong to marginally severe isolated storms remain possible Saturday afternoon. See all weather alerts here.
11/21: **This warning has been cancelled.** Additional isolated strong to marginally severe storms remain possible this afternoon. Keep an eye out for any additional NWS products!
items.desc: The NWS advises that strong to marginally severe isolated storms remain possible Saturday afternoon.

items.title: Tornado warning now canceled was issued for parts of Miami-Dade, Broward counties
items.text:
The warning was originally set to last until 12:30 p.m. Saturday.

The National Weather Service has canceled a previously issued tornado warning for northern Miami-Dade County and south central Broward County Saturday afternoon. It was scheduled to last until 12:30 p.m., but the agency canceled it minutes later.
The NWS alert said a severe thunderstorm capable of producing a tornado was located near Hialeah just before noon, with radar indicating rotation. Beyond Hialeah, areas impacted by the warning included Pembroke Pines, Miramar, Miami Gardens, North Miami, Miami Lakes, Hialeah Gardens, Opa-Locka, Miami Shores, Medley, Westview, Palm Springs North, Country Club, Miramar Parkway and University Drive, Pennsuco, Hard Rock Stadium, Golden Glades, Pinewood, West Little River, and Biscayne Park.
Residents were urged by the NWS to take cover immediately by moving to an interior room on the lowest floor of a sturdy building, avoiding windows. Anyone who was outdoors, in a mobile home, or in a car was advised to move to the closest substantial shelter.
In a message discussing the cancelation, the NWS said the thunderstorm that prompted the warning weakened below severe limits and no longer appears to be capable of producing a tornado. However, gusty winds and heavy rain are still possible.
The tornado may have produced hail that was roughly three-quarters of an inch thick.
CBS News Miami and the NEXT Weather Team will provide updates as more details are shared.
items.desc: The warning was originally set to last until 12:30 p.m. Saturday.

items.title: Here's what to catch during Design Miami this year
items.text:
From Playboy to Play-Doh, these are the things we're looking forward to this year at the fair and beyond

Design Miami is back for its 22nd edition starting 1 December. Here are the fairs, events and installations to catch while you’re there at the beach and beyond
As soon as America’s collective tryptophan hangover lifts post-Thanksgiving, the globe’s cultural cognoscenti make a beeline for Florida to attend North America’s largest confluence of art and design: Miami Art Week . The extravaganza, which takes place the first week of December, is centred primarily around two large international fairs in Miami Beach, Design Miami , an expo of global collectible design, and Art Basel Miami Beach , a major modern and contemporary art fair. Joining them are about 20 other international fairs, in addition to hundreds of events, exhibitions and installations taking place across the city. With so much to see – and so many hotspots at which to be seen – it’s easy to feel overwhelmed. Here are 10 things we’re looking forward to seeing this year, from the fair tents to the beach and beyond.
WHAT: Since it was founded in 2005, Design Miami has become the definitive destination to view collectible design en masse. Now in its 22nd edition, the fair’s influence has gone global, with satellites in Seoul , Paris and – beginning early next year – Dubai . That reach will be felt in the Miami Beach tent, with more than two dozen global galleries present. Highlights include an installation of modern tapestries by Boccara gallery; Lina Bo Bardi-designed furnishings presented by Espasso; and a fun presentation of designer-made mailboxes, courtesy AUTOBODY autobody. WHEN: 1- 6 December 2026 WHERE: Convention Center Drive and 19th Street, Miami Beach, FL 33139
WHAT: Art Basel ’s annual showing in Miami Beach is like the Super Bowl of the art world: big, expensive and a prime place to spy a celebrity or three. This year, more than 270 exhibitors from some 40 countries will congregate in the Miami Beach Convention Center, offering a dizzying array of modern and contemporary art up for grabs. If you go, be sure to catch Wallpaper* guest editor Carrie Mae Weems's latest photograph Seaside (1) at Gladstone’s booth; a surrealist garden complete with pearls and skeletons, courtesy Nina Johnson; and Zero 10, a platform devoted to digital art, featuring works by Studio DRIFT , Refik Anadol and Jon Rafman . WHEN: 4-6 December 2026 WHERE: Miami Beach Convention Center, 1901 Convention Center Drive Miami Beach, FL 33139
WHAT: Have you heard? Playboy just snapped up the Freehand Miami, with plans to convert the hotel into a private members club. Before that happens, the media and hospitality company is launching a three-day Art Week ‘residency’ called, ‘Banned’, that will explore the idea of censorship through a host of artworks by Andy Warhol, Salvador Dalí and more. Because everyone just reads Playboy for the art, right? WHEN: 4-5 December 2026 WHERE: 1688 Jefferson Ave, Miami Beach, FL 33139
WHAT: The locus of Design Miami is, of course, the tent. But the fair’s annual Design District commission is a reminder that there’s so much to see beyond Miami Beach. This year, the site-specific installation will be by Objects of Common Interest , a New York - and Athens -based design firm founded by Eleni Petaloti and Leonidas Trampoukis.
